properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent and no option is preferred.

ANTHONY, 2026-09-10: *"how in this design effort, that the agent has try out every tool and skill prior to updating anything about it. If you're calling the wrong tool, then why would in another project, would an agent not also do the same? This is actually a very big deal for me that we've gone back to the agent using grep and not reflow2 where appropriate."*

═══ ⭐ WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HELD, READ AFTER HE SAID SO AND BEFORE THIS NODE WAS FINISHED ═══

This question is NOT new here and this node must not read as if it were. `topic_report` on adoption returned 20 nodes across 7 types. The load-bearing ones:

· `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (ACCEPTED) — "Skill use is triggered by the SITUATION, not remembered — and THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER." The standing intent this whole question sits under.
· `fact:a-skill-is-loaded-only-when-something-already-in-hand-demands-it` (2026-08-28, root_cause) — an agent loads a skill when something already in hand makes it a precondition, "and otherwise substantially not at all".
· `fact:agents-do-self-invoke-skills-at-scale-and-the-hook-not-the-catalogue-predicts-which` (2026-08-29, n=93 sessions, 5,680 reflow2 calls) — REFUTES THE STRONG FORM OF THE ABOVE. 88% of skill loads had no slash command behind them; agents self-invoke constantly. The WEAK form survives: loading is driven by AN INSTRUCTION ALREADY IN CONTEXT.
· `dec:idea-where-does-tool-use-actually-fail-four-layers` — the four-layer diagnostic this all hangs off.
· `dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered` — the same question for one specific discipline, written into five skills and still depending on somebody loading one.
· `dec:the-graph-asks-what-a-session-made-false` (ACCEPTED) — "BUILD THE TWO MISSING LEGS, NOT A SEVENTH MECHANISM."
· `fact:reflow2s-mechanisms-for-reaching-an-agent-are-mostly-claude-code-shaped`, and `rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground`, which bound where any answer may live.

═══ ⭐⭐ AND THE 93-SESSION MEASUREMENT NAMES THE LEVER, WHICH CHANGES THIS NODE'S OPTIONS ═══

    skill            loads   /cmd typed   ratio
    where-am-i          42        5        8.4x   ← THE ONLY WORKING SKILL NAMED IN THE SessionStart HOOK
    brainstorm          22       10        2.2x
    capture-session     19       18        1.1x
    link-artifacts      15        0         —

Its own conclusion: the MCP instructions name ALL 23 skills and usage across them runs 42..0, so A CATALOGUE THAT LISTS EVERYTHING PREDICTS NOTHING; the SessionStart hook names three, and the one of those with a recurring situation is the most-loaded skill in the set by a factor of two.

⭐ TODAY FITS THAT EXACTLY, WHICH IS WHY IT IS EVIDENCE AND NOT JUST AN APOLOGY. The 2026-09-10 SessionStart hook named `open_questions`, `where-am-i`, `loop_status`, `unclaimed_findings`, `link-artifacts`, `detect-and-ask` — EVERY ONE OF WHICH THIS SESSION USED, most of them repeatedly. It did not name `find_tools`, which was not called once across a whole day of changing the tool surface it indexes. That is also the cheapest available test of the confound the measurement names against itself (is it the hook, or is `where-am-i` simply the most useful skill?): `find_tools` was intrinsically useful for exactly this job and still went untouched.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none preferred ═══

(g) NAME THE TOOL IN THE ALWAYS-INJECTED HOOK — the option the evidence actually points at, and the one absent before the prior work was read. It is also the discriminating experiment `fact:agents-do-self-invoke...` explicitly asks for: "a second skill added to the hook would test it, and that is the cheap discriminating experiment." Adding `find_tools` would both plausibly fix the behaviour AND settle the hook-versus-usefulness confound. ⚠️ The hook is finite and every addition dilutes it; a hook that names everything becomes the catalogue that predicts nothing.

(a) NOTHING. The instructions already say to search before writing and to run `find_tools` before reporting a tool missing. Cheapest, and the option to beat — but it is what was in place on the day it failed, and the 93-session data says a catalogue is the weakest surface there is.

(b) A WRITTEN DISCIPLINE: exercise a tool as a consumer before changing it. ⚠️ THE EVIDENCE IS AGAINST THIS ONE. Passive hints measured 0 acted-on against 3 obeyed blocks, and it is the step-② shape `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` says is invisible when skipped.

(c) A MECHANICAL GATE on changes touching a tool's description or parameters. Verifiable, unlike (b). ⚠️ Hollow to satisfy: calling a tool once proves nothing about whether it was FINDABLE, which is the failure that occurred.

(d) MEASURE THE SURFACE RATHER THAN THE AGENT — ask `find_tools` a corpus of user-phrased questions and score whether the right tool comes back. Turns the question into a number that moves. ⚠️ Its trap was measured on this design the same week: whoever writes the questions writes ones the current descriptions happen to answer, a fit validated by its own fitting set. The questions must come from the FIELD REPORTS, where users already wrote what they were trying to do before knowing which tool to call.

(e) PUT BEHAVIOURAL INVARIANTS IN THE DESCRIPTION. `record_change` refuses to record history into a `planned` epoch and its served description says "planned" zero times, so a consumer learns it only by being refused. Narrowest true statement; does not generalise to "the agent reached for grep".

(f) REMOVE THE CRUTCH FOR ONE PIECE OF WORK — one change to the tool surface with the source deliberately out of reach. Produces evidence no instruction can, once rather than standing.

═══ 🛑 COUNTER-ARGUMENTS ═══

⚠️ **"NOT A SEVENTH MECHANISM."** `dec:the-graph-asks-what-a-session-made-false` settled a neighbouring case by building the two MISSING LEGS of an existing mechanism rather than adding another. Options (b), (c) and (d) are all new mechanisms; (g) is a missing leg of one that demonstrably works. That asymmetry should count.

⚠️ "EVERY TOOL AND SKILL" IS LARGER THAN IT SOUNDS: 180 tools, 23 skills. Exercising all of them before any change is not a discipline anyone keeps, and a rule nobody keeps is worse than none. Scoped to THE TOOL BEING CHANGED it is keepable.

⚠️ THE BUILDER'S SOURCE ACCESS IS GENUINELY USEFUL. The problem is not that the source was read; it is that the surface was never tried FIRST, so its failure produced no signal. Any option should preserve the reading and add the trying.

⚠️ AND THE HONEST LIMIT OF ALL SEVEN: none makes a lexical catalogue able to tell a claim from its denial. `find_tools` ranked the NEGATION of the query. Every option here would surface that sooner without fixing it, and that is the question `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` has carried since 2026-08-01.

═══ WHAT THIS NODE ADDS, AFTER ALL THAT ═══

One thing, and it is the thing the prior work says it does NOT cover. `fact:a-skill-is-loaded-only-when-something-already-in-hand-demands-it` states in its own limits: *"It says nothing about consumers. Both observed sessions had far more reflow2 context than any consumer's agent will have, which makes them a BEST case."* THE ASYMMETRY IS THAT GAP: a reflow2 developer who hits a surface failure pays nothing, because the source is one grep away, SO THE FAILURE IS NEVER FILED. A consumer pays the task and has no second channel to notice. The crutch does not merely mask the defect — it removes the feedback that would report it.
properties.name: OPEN — should a session USE a tool as a consumer would before changing it? The builder's grep is a crutch no consumer has, so the surface can fail him for free and he never files it
properties.rationale: Anthony's question, then his correction that the graph already held the discussion — which it did, across 20 nodes including an accepted requirement, a root cause, and a 93-session measurement that refutes that root cause's strong form and names the actual lever: a skill or tool named in the always-injected SessionStart hook gets used, a catalogue listing everything predicts nothing. Today fits that cleanly — every hook-named tool was used, find_tools was not named and was not called once. That adds option (g), which is both the evidence-backed repair and the discriminating experiment the measurement itself asks for. The one thing this node contributes rather than repeats is the consumer asymmetry, which the root cause explicitly excludes from its own scope.
